question:
A 36-year-old man presents with complaints of left hip and low back pain. He reports that the pain
began after a 6-hour flight when visiting family last week. On physical examination, the anterior
superior iliac spine (ASIS) compression test shows decreased resistance on the right. The posterior
superior iliac spine (PSIS) is found to be more inferior on the left, while the right ASIS is more inferior
compared to the left. The pubic rami are symmetrical. Which of the following is the best positioning to
treat this patient using muscle energy? Answer Choices: (A) Patient lying supine, physician's hand on
his right ASIS, and his left hip and knee flexed, supported against the physician (B) Patient lying prone,
physician's hand on his left ASIS, and his right lower extremity internally rotated with resistance applied
(C) Patient lying prone, physician's hand on his right PSIS, and his left lower extremity extended with
resistance applied (D) Patient lying supine with his right hip flexed, abducted, and externally rotated (E)
Patient lying supine, physician's hand on his right ASIS, and his left lower extremity extended and
adducted (F) Patient lying supine, physician's hand on his left PSIS, and his right lower extremity
abducted and externally rotated (G) Patient lying prone, physician's hand on his right ASIS, and his left
lower extremity abducted and internally rotated (H) Patient lying supine, physician's hand on his left
ASIS, and his right lower extremity slightly abducted and off the table (I) Patient lying supine,
physician's hand on his right ASIS, and his left lower extremity slightly abducted and off the table (J)
Patient lying supine, physician's hand on his left ASIS, and his right hip and knee flexed, supported
against the physician
 A. Patient lying supine, physician's hand on his left ASIS, and his right lower extremity slightly
abducted and off the table
B. Patient lying supine with his right hip flexed, abducted, and externally rotated
C. Patient lying supine, physician's hand on his left ASIS, and his right hip and knee flexed,
supported against the physician
D. Patient lying supine, physician's hand on his right ASIS, and his left lower extremity extended and
adducted
E. Patient lying supine, physician's hand on his right ASIS, and his left hip and knee flexed,
supported against the physician
F. Patient lying prone, physician's hand on his right PSIS, and his left lower extremity extended with
resistance applied
G. Patient lying prone, physician's hand on his right ASIS, and his left lower extremity abducted and
internally rotated
H. Patient lying supine, physician's hand on his left PSIS, and his right lower extremity abducted and
externally rotated
I. Patient lying supine, physician's hand on his right ASIS, and his left lower extremity slightly
abducted and off the table
J. Patient lying prone, physician's hand on his left ASIS, and his right lower extremity internally
rotated with resistance applied
